summary: Get started with the source checkout that is available today, choose a theme preset or skip the first-run choices, learn the Studio rooms, and bring a file into the Library. Bunzai does not currently have a published release, so this walkthrough points to the pinned Bun version and recursive submodule setup. The wizard can be revisited through Settings only for the choices the Studio retains; it does not limit what you can create. The Library receipt lets you choose which parsed pieces to keep before import writes them. Its separate Start fresh door creates a blank character. A provider is only needed when you submit a scene turn, not for local import, editing, or conversion.

sections.title: The short version
sections.summary: There is no published Bunzai release yet. The available path is a source checkout using Bun 1.3.14: clone with recursive submodules, install the lockfile dependencies, and run the local Studio with bun run dev. The server prints its loopback address, normally 127.0.0.1:8321. A new studio opens the first-run wizard and then the Library, where you can import a supported file or create a blank character. See the illustrated installation guide for platform-specific Bun instructions, backups, updates, and troubleshooting.

sections.title: The first-run wizard
sections.summary: The first-run wizard appears when a studio has no completed setup. It asks which theme preset to use, which kinds of pieces you want to make, where you expect to publish, and which accent color to use. RoleCall is the default theme, with Theater, Paper, and GirliePop also available. The first selected kind controls the initial Library deck; Characters is the fallback. Publish targets come from the formats Bunzai knows, and Not sure keeps the defaults ready. Skip all fills remaining defaults and proceeds to the closing screen. Retained setup choices can be changed later in Settings.

sections.title: The Dock
sections.summary: The Dock gathers the everyday Studio rooms. In the RoleCall workspace shown in the guide, it runs along the bottom of the Studio. Workbench edits pieces, Library browses and imports them, and Press exports only items you stage to a selected target. Settings stays reachable from the Dock. Specialist tools such as Docs and CSS Workshop are available from the app catalog rather than appearing as everyday Dock tiles. The configured home app controls a normal launch, and the Studio tries to restore the active room after reload.

sections.title: Bringing in your first file
sections.summary: When the Library is empty, use its import door to drop a supported file or choose one from the file picker. The Studio reads files before it writes anything and presents a receipt showing parsed pieces. Readable pieces are selected by default; uncheck anything you do not want to keep. Import writes only the pieces still checked. Add more files appends another batch, while Not now closes without importing. The empty Library has a separate Start fresh door that creates and saves a blank character, then opens it in Workbench. Use that path when you want a clean starting point rather than importing a file.

sections.title: Tips
sections.summary: No release is published yet, so use the pinned source installation. Skip all fills the wizard defaults; retained choices remain editable. The first selected kind sets the initial Library deck. If an import receipt says a file could not be read, it may be unsupported, malformed, or damaged. The formats command lists available adapters, and the CLI UI command accepts a custom studio folder.
